conceptDrafts.logline: An ordained divorce mediator agrees to officiate her ex-husband's wedding to her half-sister — over one rehearsal weekend where every toast, seating chart, and vow draft reopens the file on who left whom.

settings.vibe: banquet-hall crossfire, smiling through clenched teeth

concept.summary: Ruth Adler — divorce mediator, ordained online as a joke that stopped being funny — is asked to officiate the wedding of Marcus (her ex-husband) to Piper (her half-sister, eleven years younger, same mother). The rehearsal weekend at the family lake house also gathers Gene (Ruth's stepfather, who is ALSO Marcus's business partner) and Sadie (Marcus's nineteen-year-old daughter from his first marriage — Ruth's former stepdaughter, who still calls Ruth 'mom' when nobody's listening). Ruth wrote her own divorce settlement; now she has to write their vows.
themes: who gets custody of a family

characters.name: Ruth Adler
characters.backstory: Built a practice untangling other people's marriages after failing to untangle her own.
characters.motivations: Prove — publicly, ceremonially — that she is fine.
characters.flaws: Treats every conversation as a negotiation to be won calmly.
characters.want: Officiate flawlessly and leave Sunday with the moral high ground.
characters.need: To stop billing her grief by the hour.

relationships.description: ex-husband (divorced 4 years; she drafted the settlement herself)
half-sister — same mother, eleven years younger; the bride
stepfather (married Ruth's mother when Ruth was 15)
former stepdaughter from Marcus's first marriage; Sadie still calls her 'mom' in private

characters.voice: mediation-speak weaponized; 'what I'm hearing is…' as a knife
characters.arc: From performing neutrality to filing her own grievance out loud.

characters.name: Marcus Hale
characters.backstory: Divorced twice; co-owns a marina franchise with Gene.
characters.motivations: Get through the weekend without a single raised voice.
characters.need: To say one true thing before the vows.

relationships.description: ex-wife; asked her to officiate believing it would 'close the loop'
fiancée — met at Ruth's mother's funeral
business partner in the marina franchise
daughter from his FIRST marriage (not Ruth's biological child)

characters.voice: agreeable to the point of vanishing; apologizes mid-sentence

characters.name: Piper Voss
characters.backstory: Grew up hearing Ruth held up as the standard; kept the surname of the father Ruth never shared.
characters.motivations: One event where she is not the footnote.
characters.flaws: Confuses being envied with being loved.
characters.want: Ruth's blessing, in front of everyone, in the vows Ruth writes.
characters.need: To want the marriage more than the optics of it.

relationships.description: half-sister — same mother, different fathers; kept her own father's surname (Voss)
stepfather to Ruth only — Gene arrived after Piper's father; to Piper he is 'mom's second husband', not a parent

characters.name: Gene Kessler
characters.backstory: Married the girls' mother; buried her two years ago; has been hosting holidays out of momentum since.
characters.motivations: Keep the family assembled at any cost, including honesty.
characters.flaws: Uses the marina partnership to keep Marcus in the family like a lien.
characters.want: The wedding to go perfectly at HIS lake house.
characters.need: To admit the family he's preserving dissolved two years ago.

relationships.description: stepdaughter (he raised her from 15; walked her down the aisle at her wedding to Marcus)
business partner AND former son-in-law — soon to be son-in-law again via Piper
his late wife's younger daughter; never formally his step-anything and both of them know it

characters.voice: toastmaster boom with a two-second delay where doubt lives

characters.name: Sadie Hale
characters.backstory: Nineteen; Marcus's daughter from his first marriage to Dana (absent, alive, unmentioned at events). Ruth raised her ages 8–15.
characters.motivations: Make someone say ONE accurate sentence about this family out loud.
characters.want: Maid of honor toast that tells the truth.
characters.need: Permission to keep loving Ruth without betraying Piper's day.

relationships.description: former stepmother, functionally her mother ages 8–15; still calls her 'mom' privately
future stepmother, six years older than her; they follow each other and like nothing

characters.voice: gen-z deposition style; quotes people back verbatim with timestamps

beats.name: The Ask
beats.summary: Marcus and Piper ask Ruth to officiate; Ruth says yes before either finishes the sentence, to win the moment.
beats.purpose: Establish Ruth performing 'fine' as a competitive sport.

beats.name: Seating Chart Summit
beats.summary: Gene's seating chart puts Ruth at the family table between Sadie and the empty chair kept for the girls' late mother; Ruth re-drafts it like a settlement exhibit and Sadie photographs both versions.
beats.purpose: The audience sees the family's real fault lines drawn in table assignments — and Sadie building her receipts file.

beats.name: Vow Draft One
beats.summary: Piper rejects Ruth's first vow draft as 'a contract'; Ruth rewrites it warmer and realizes she's quoting her own wedding vows to Marcus.
beats.purpose: Ruth's professional armor cracks along the exact seam of the old marriage.

beats.name: Rehearsal Toast
beats.summary: Sadie's practice toast quotes, verbatim with dates, three family lies from the weekend; Gene cuts the mic and Marcus, for once, doesn't smooth it over.
beats.purpose: The receipts detonate; Marcus's silence breaks where we expected Ruth's to.
